newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia housing recovery slipping - industry.
newsitem.headline: Australia housing recovery slipping - industry.

text.p: Australian building industry groups on Wednesday warned that a fall in the number of building approvals in June showed the momentum of the housing recovery was slowing.

"These declines show that the gathering momentum of the housing recovery evident earlier this year may be slipping away," Master Builders Australia national deputy executive director Wilhelm Harnisch said in a statement.
Dwelling unit building approvals fell a seasonally-adjusted 4.5 percent in June to 11,774 from a revised 12,325 in May, compared with 10,225 in June 1996.
Harnisch said he was concerned that the effects of past interest rate cuts may be waning.
He said the Reserve Bank of Australia, which cut official cash rates by 0.5 percentage points to 5.0 percent earlier on Wednesday, might still need to consider further action.
"(It) may need to cut once again if the pace of economic growth remains sluggish," he said.
Housing Industry Association Ltd managing director Ron Silberberg said Wednesday's building approvals figures showed the pace of recovery in the housing industry had eased.
He welcomed the latest interest rate cut, saying it was needed to help boost confidence and sustain the momentum of the recovery.

"Australia's record low inflation rate, coupled with this cut in official interest rates, will continue to make housing an attractive and affordable investment for all Australians," Silberberg said in a statement.
Before today's cut, the Reserve Bank previously eased monetary policy four times between July last year and May 23, cutting rates by 0.5 percentage points each time.
